headline_marked: [[Egg price hits nearly Tk 15 per piece]] in Dhaka markets, dozen now Tk 180-190
headline: Egg price hits nearly Tk 15 per piece in Dhaka markets, dozen now Tk 180-190
summary: The surge makes eggs an increasingly unaffordable protein source for low-income families, who also face broiler chicken prices around Tk 200/kg for two months.
details: Egg prices have seen a further increase across Dhaka markets. A half-dozen of brown farm eggs now costs Tk 50 in large markets, while neighborhood grocery stores are selling them for Tk 55.

For low-income families who typically purchase eggs individually, each egg is now priced at approximately Tk 15. Eggs and broiler chicken are crucial protein sources for low and middle-income populations in Bangladesh.
A full dozen of eggs is currently retailing between Tk 180 and Tk 190. This represents an increase of around Tk 10 per dozen just within the last week.
Producers attribute the price hike to rising feed costs, stating that one kilogram of feed is required to produce six eggs. The price of feed per kilogram has reportedly increased by up to Tk 12.

White farm eggs are available for Tk 145-155 per dozen, and duck eggs are selling for Tk 190-200 per dozen. Meanwhile, broiler chicken prices have remained steady at around Tk 200 per kilogram for the past two months.

headline: Indian pilot hailed as hero after saving flydubai plane from co-pilot's crash attempt
summary: An Indian pilot, stabbed by his co-pilot, managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene and prevent a flydubai plane from crashing after it plunged 14,000 feet.
details: Leaders from Israel and India have praised Indian pilot Smit Machchhar as a hero after he saved 174 lives on a flydubai flight. His co-pilot allegedly stabbed him in an attempt to crash the plane on Wednesday.

The incident occurred mid-flight from the UAE to Israel, causing the jet to plunge nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. Despite being covered in blood, Machchhar managed to click the release to open the cockpit door.
This allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot. Two other flydubai pilots on board then took control and safely landed the aircraft in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and Indian PM Narendra Modi lauded Machchhar's immense courage. Netanyahu stated all passengers, including Israeli citizens, were out of harm's way.
Machchhar, who hails from Mumbai, underwent surgery and is now reported to be in stable condition, receiving medical attention in Tabuk. Indian authorities are in touch with his family.
Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel pending an investigation into the altercation's cause, warning against premature speculation. Saudi authorities will interrogate the co-pilot.
caption:
A flydubai flight plunged 14,000 feet after a co-pilot stabbed the pilot in an attempted crash. An Indian pilot's bravery saved 174 lives.

Leaders from Israel and India have praised Indian pilot Smit Machchhar as a hero after he saved 174 lives on a flydubai flight. His co-pilot allegedly stabbed him in an attempt to crash the plane on Wednesday.

The incident occurred mid-flight from the UAE to Israel, causing the jet to plunge nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. Despite being covered in blood, Machchhar managed to click the release to open the cockpit door.

This allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot. Two other flydubai pilots on board then took control and safely landed the aircraft in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and Indian PM Narendra Modi lauded Machchhar's immense courage. Netanyahu stated all passengers, including Israeli citizens, were out of harm's way.

Machchhar, who hails from Mumbai, underwent surgery and is now reported to be in stable condition, receiving medical attention in Tabuk. Indian authorities are in touch with his family.

Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel pending an investigation into the altercation's cause, warning against premature speculation. Saudi authorities will interrogate the co-pilot.
